frontmatter_description: Diagnose when the core issue is shaping the impression other people form through self-description, disclosure order, or image management.
title: Self-Presentation and Impression Management
use_when: Use when the question is about what image the person wants others to form.
Use when the key choice is how to present self-information, order disclosures, or describe oneself.
Use when the main task is managing how one is seen, not whether the information is private or true.
Use when the scene asks what to reveal first, what to emphasize, or how to frame identity for an audience.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the main issue is whether information should remain private; use privacy and boundaries instead.
Do not use when the main issue is apology, repair, or easing hurt after harm; use relationship repair instead.
Do not use when the main issue is negotiation, compromise, or mutual adjustment; use joint plan skills instead.
Do not use when the main issue is power, hierarchy, escalation, or deference across rank; use power navigation instead.
Do not use when the question is about true emotion display versus concealment; that is emotional inference or display, not overall image management.
decision_variable: the desired impression others should form
trigger_checklist: Is the answer about how the person wants to be seen?
Is the key lever what to say first, omit, emphasize, or frame?
Is the content about identity presentation rather than fact detection?
Would changing the order or tone of self-disclosure change the social image?
Is the issue broad self-image, not one protected secret or one apology?
workflow: Identify the audience and the social goal of the presentation.
Ask what impression the speaker wants to create or protect.
Check whether the choice is about disclosure order, framing, or self-description.
Ignore the factual truth question unless deception is the main issue.
Choose the option that best fits the intended image.

special_case.title: Image management with truthful disclosure
special_case.rule: Truthful statements can still be impression management if the question is about which facts to lead with, how to frame them, or which identity to signal.

worked_example.scene: A job candidate lists volunteer work before test scores in a self-introduction.
worked_example.question: Why did they choose that order?
worked_example.answer_logic: The decision is driven by the image they want to project first, so this is self-presentation rather than privacy, repair, or lying.

boundary_exit_rule: If the core question becomes whether information should be shared at all, exit to privacy and boundaries (micro-48).
If the core question becomes how to respond after offense or damage, exit to repair and apology (micro-49).
If the core question becomes what action best satisfies both sides, exit to negotiation or joint planning (micro-51).
If the core question becomes what a superior or subordinate should say, exit to power navigation (micro-52).
If the core question becomes what emotion is actually being felt or shown, exit to emotion inference (micro-28 / micro-29).
If the scene is a full first-impression or formal-interaction prototype rather than a single self-presentation diagnostic, route up to macro-19 and use this micro only as expansion.

references.route_signal: Use this micro unit when the scene asks how a person manages self-image, disclosure order, or self-description to shape others' impressions.
hard_boundary: Privacy is about whether information may be shared; this unit is about how to present self-information once presentation is in view.
Repair is about fixing harm after a social break; this unit is about image before or apart from repair.
Power navigation is about strategy under hierarchy; this unit is about the image being projected, not rank-based tactics.
Emotional display concerns visible feeling; this unit concerns the broader social picture of the self.
shortcut_to_avoid: Do not equate impression management with lying; truthful framing can still be self-presentation.
Do not use secrecy as the default answer; secrecy may serve image, but the variable is the intended impression.
Do not overfocus on single emotion cues; the unit is about overall self-image, not expression decoding.
common_failure_modes: Confusing image management with privacy control.
Treating apology or repair as if it were self-presentation.
Assuming any selective disclosure is deception.
Missing that disclosure order alone can be the diagnostic clue.

minimal_pair.case: A person introduces themselves by leading with leadership experience instead of a recent job gap.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: The choice is driven by the impression they want others to form from the self-description.

minimal_pair.case: A person refuses to tell friends a confidential medical detail.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: This is primarily about whether the information should be shared, so it belongs to privacy and boundaries.

boundary_stress_test: If the person could say the same facts in a different order and change the impression, this unit may apply.
If the main goal is to protect a secret rather than shape a public image, this unit should not be used.
If the scene adds apology, blame, or reconciliation, the center of gravity has moved out of this unit.
references.generalization_note: This unit covers bios, introductions, first impressions, selective disclosure, and framing choices whenever the primary variable is the impression others should form.

validation_seed.positive_pattern: The speaker chooses what to reveal first in order to look competent, trustworthy, or likable.
validation_seed.near_miss_pattern: The speaker hides a fact because it is private, but the question is really about disclosure permission.
validation_seed.boundary_pattern: The speaker apologizes after upsetting someone, and the task is to repair the relationship.

notes: Keep the unit narrow: image management only, not all communication strategy.
Do not absorb privacy, repair, persuasion, or hierarchy into this skill.
A good diagnostic cue is the question 'What impression should others get?'
core_question: Manage self-information, image, disclosure order, and self-description
